parsed.main_gap: The set Q is defined as the primes dividing A, which makes the central Lemma false; the argument only works (and is written) for Q = all primes at most A.

errors.description: Definition of Q is wrong: with Q = primes dividing A the key Lemma fails. For A=15 the terms are 15,18,20,24,...; sigma(18)={3}, but {3} misses P(20)={2,5}, so sigma(18) is not good. The write-up's own 'falsification' section states the correct set ('all primes at most A'), so this is an internally contradictory slip, repairable by replacing Q with {p prime, p<=A} (then L is the primorial).
errors.quote:
Q=\{p:p\text{ is prime and }p\mid A\},
\qquad
\sigma(x)=P(x)\cap Q.

errors.description: Key step of the Lemma's proof is invalid under the stated definition of Q: primes dividing x but not dividing A need not exceed A (e.g. x=20, A=15, prime 2). The step is correct only for Q = primes <= A, confirming the definitional slip.
errors.quote: Every prime in \(\sigma(b)\) is at most \(A\), whereas every prime in \(P(x)\setminus\sigma(x)\) is greater than \(A\).

errors.description: Non sequitur justification: sharing a prime factor with A only gives sigma(x) nonempty, not that the primes dividing A suffice; this claim is explicitly contradicted by the author's own item 1 in the discussion.
errors.quote: Only the primes dividing \(A\) can matter here, because every term shares a prime factor with \(A=a_1\).

parsed.notes: Apart from the Q slip, the architecture is fully correct: characterization (1), the descent construction Rp^k with the minimality bound, the strong induction, upward closure, and the exact-count argument giving a_{n+T}=a_n+L for all n from the threshold A.
